result.rule: When The description says that each produced part must be verified by its own check before a later step, and that a failed check requires rework of that part before the process can continue.: Model each verification as its own activity after the production activity it checks. Follow it with an exclusive gateway whose outgoing flows carry the success condition (continuing to the next step) and the failure condition (returning to the rework activity). Do not fold the verification into the production activity or omit the decision.

When the description lists several activities in a stated order, with transitional phrases such as 'Next', 'then', or 'as soon as', and one activity is followed by a later activity or check that the description places after it: Model each described activity as its own task, and connect each one to the activity the description places immediately after it with a sequence flow. Do not leave a described successor without an incoming flow from its predecessor, even when the predecessor is a simple selection or a task that follows another task. Where the description adds a later step that follows an earlier one, add that flow as well, so that every stated step is reachable in the order given.

When the description lists two or more actions that must each be carried out, such as notifying different parties, without stating an order between them, and the process continues only after all of them are done: Model each such action as its own branch that starts from a parallel gateway, and join the branches with a parallel gateway before the next step. Do not use an exclusive gateway, and do not add conditions to these branches.

When the description says that several activities or item branches start at the same time after one point, and that a following step begins once the first of the concurrently arriving items is available, while the remaining items keep arriving in an unspecified order and must not hold up that step: Open the concurrent activities and item branches with a parallel gateway split placed before them, with one outgoing flow per branch and no conditions on those flows. Model the junction before the first-arrival step as a complex gateway that continues on the first incoming token, not as a parallel join that waits for every branch. Keep the handling of the remaining arrivals on their own branches, linked to the process so they do not block the continuation.
